records.issue_text: desktop/topic-post.scss read-state link light-scheme value inverted from 30% to 70%, washing out light-theme reply/read-state links instead of only affecting dark themes
records.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss`, the diff changes the bold link color from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. That makes the light-scheme branch (first argument) use 70% lightness instead of the previous 30%, while the dark-scheme branch uses 30%. This matches the finding’s claim that the light/dark values are inverted and would likely wash out the link color in the light theme.

records.issue_text: mobile/modal.scss .custom-message-length light value inverted from 70% to 30%, diverging from its desktop twin and giving mobile light users near-black hint text
records.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss`, `.custom-message-length` changed from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%);` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%));`. This makes the *light* theme use `$primary` at 30% lightness (much darker) instead of 70%, while `desktop/modal.scss` uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%));`. The mobile version appears inverted relative to desktop and likely produces overly dark hint text for light users.
